```{r load-libs}
library(RLT)
```

## Overview

This page demonstrates uncertainty bands for the conditional survival curve at chosen predictor values. These describe uncertainty about the curve, not a prediction interval for an individual's event time. The example uses the smoothed approach in `get.surv.band()`.

Assess how much information supports each estimated curve:

- Target predictor values should be represented in the training data, especially for the important variables, to limit extrapolation.
- Inspect the number of observations still at risk over time. The far tail has less support when few observations remain under follow-up without an event.

## Data

We simulate right-censored survival data from a proportional hazards model. The first and third predictors carry signal; the rest are noise.

```{r data-prep}
set.seed(2)

n <- 200
p <- 10
X <- matrix(rnorm(n * p), n, p)
colnames(X) <- paste0("X", seq_len(p))

xlink <- function(x) exp(x[, 1] + x[, 3] / 2)
FT <- rexp(n, rate = xlink(X))
CT <- pmin(6, rexp(n, rate = 0.25))

Y <- pmin(FT, CT)
Censor <- as.numeric(FT <= CT)
```

## Target Points

We choose two target points at interior quantiles of the important variables `X1` and `X3`. The remaining variables are fixed at their training medians.

```{r target-points}
target_base <- apply(X, 2, median)
testX <- matrix(rep(target_base, times = 2), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)
colnames(testX) <- colnames(X)

testX[, 1] <- quantile(X[, 1], probs = c(0.35, 0.65))
testX[, 3] <- quantile(X[, 3], probs = c(0.35, 0.65))

rownames(testX) <- c("Interior lower-risk target", "Interior higher-risk target")
testX[, c(1, 3)]
```

## Fit and Predict with Variance

We use `var.mode = "matched"` to estimate the covariance of the predicted cumulative hazard over time, which is the scale used by the confidence-band calculation. Matched mode requires an even number of trees and uses paired half-samples without replacement. Here the 1,000 trees form 500 pairs; the required sampling settings are explicit in the call. This mode automatically enables distributed importance when `importance = FALSE`.

```{r fit-predict}
fit <- RLT(
  X, Y, Censor, model = "survival",
  ntrees = 1000, mtry = min(p, 10), nmin = 5,
  nsplit = 3,
  resample.prob = 0.5, resample.replace = FALSE,
  importance = FALSE, verbose = FALSE,
  ncores = 1,
  var.mode = "matched",
  split.rule = "logrank"
)

RLTPred <- predict(fit, testX, var.est = TRUE, ncores = 1)
```

## Choose a Display Range

The prediction object includes the full observed failure-time grid. For this example, we display only $t \leq 2$ and report the smallest risk-set count in that range. Time 2 is a display choice, not a validated threshold for adequate support. The band below is still constructed using every time in `RLTPred$timepoints`.

```{r supported-time}
risk_set <- vapply(RLTPred$timepoints, function(t) sum(Y >= t), integer(1))
plot_time_max <- 2
plot_id <- which(RLTPred$timepoints <= plot_time_max)

if (length(plot_id) == 0) {
  plot_id <- 1
}

list(
  Plot_Time_Range = "t <= 2",
  Minimum_At_Risk_in_Plotted_Range = min(risk_set[plot_id]),
  Number_of_Plotted_Timepoints = length(plot_id)
)
```

## Simultaneous Confidence Band

With `alpha = 0.05`, `get.surv.band()` constructs a nominal 95% simultaneous band for the conditional survival curve over the returned time grid. The default `i = 0` returns a separate band for each target point; the nominal coverage applies to each curve separately, not jointly across the two targets or over every time between grid points.

The computed reference curve is `exp(-RLTPred$CHF)`. The function first constructs a band around `RLTPred$CHF` on the cumulative-hazard scale, then transforms its limits to the survival scale. For an ordinary survival forest the reference curve equals the returned `$Survival`; linear combination forests instead return the mean of tree product-limit curves, whose sampling variation is not directly estimated by this CHF-based calculation.

The smoothed approach uses a low-rank covariance approximation and a residual correction to form the marginal standardizing scales. Here `k_rank = 10` allows up to ten components in that approximation. The Gaussian simulations retain the original supplied covariance. The `nsim` simulations estimate the critical value needed for simultaneous coverage over the grid.

```{r band-calc}
SurvBand <- get.surv.band(RLTPred, alpha = 0.05, approach = "smoothed",
                          k_rank = 10, nsim = 5000)
```

```{r band-plot, fig.height=4.5, out.width=if (knitr::is_html_output()) 768 else "90%", out.height=if (knitr::is_html_output()) 432 else NULL, fig.alt="Two panels show survival probability against time up to 2 for interior lower-risk and higher-risk targets. Each has a black stepped estimate exp(-CHF), a red dashed true survival curve, and a shaded blue simultaneous 95 percent confidence band. Survival declines faster for the higher-risk target."}
par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))

for (i in seq_len(nrow(testX))) {
  tp <- RLTPred$timepoints[plot_id]
  S <- exp(-as.numeric(RLTPred$CHF[i, plot_id]))
  truth <- exp(-xlink(testX)[i] * tp)

  b_lower <- pmin(pmax(as.numeric(SurvBand[[i]]$lower)[plot_id], 0), 1)
  b_upper <- pmin(pmax(as.numeric(SurvBand[[i]]$upper)[plot_id], 0), 1)

  plot(tp, S, type = "n", ylim = c(0, 1),
       xlab = "Time", ylab = "Survival Probability",
       main = rownames(testX)[i])

  polygon(c(tp, rev(tp)), c(b_lower, rev(b_upper)),
          col = rgb(0.23, 0.51, 0.96, 0.25), border = NA)

  lines(tp, truth, col = "#E41A1C", lwd = 2, lty = 2)
  lines(tp, S, type = "s", lwd = 2)

  legend("topright",
         legend = c("Estimated S(t)", "True S(t)", "Simultaneous 95% Band"),
         lty = c(1, 2, NA), lwd = c(2, 2, NA),
         col = c("black", "#E41A1C", NA),
         fill = c(NA, NA, rgb(0.23, 0.51, 0.96, 0.35)),
         border = c(NA, NA, NA),
         bty = "n", cex = 0.75)
}

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

The higher-risk target has larger values of both signal variables, so its true survival curve falls faster. The black curve is the estimate `exp(-RLTPred$CHF)` of the conditional survival curve, and the shaded band describes uncertainty about that target curve. A nominal 95% simultaneous band need not contain the true curve in every simulated dataset; this one simulation does not establish coverage. Each band was constructed on the full returned grid, with only the portion through time 2 displayed here.

## Optional Rank Selection

The rank controls the covariance approximation used for the marginal scales. Instead of a fixed `k_rank`, the smoothed approach can choose it by cumulative eigenvalue proportion:

```r
SurvBand_prop <- get.surv.band(
  RLTPred, alpha = 0.05,
  approach = "smoothed",
  k_mode = "proportion",
  k_prop = 0.95
)
```

Increasing `nsim` reduces Monte Carlo variability in the estimated critical value at the cost of runtime. It does not change the fitted forest or the supplied covariance used in simulation. See `get.surv.band()` for the smoothing details and the fallback to the naive calculation with fewer than three time points.
